arc: hook → stat (30:00 vs 6 weeks) → problem ×6 (requirements pile up, iso IT estate, Salesforce change chain, without breaking, gets stuck, multiple platforms, undocumented, everything else) → reveal (logo) → feature ×4 (composer, agent transcript, architecture diagram, change timeline) → data (agent trace) → benefit → logo → cta

scenes.title: Tumbling orbit rings behind a word-by-word headline
scenes.summary: On a near-white background three thin 3D rings (one solid, one dotted, one dashed) tumble and roll through each other, their slate-to-teal colour gradient fixed left to right across the screen. From about 1s, "Sales closed the customer in" builds up word by word in the centre. Each word blurs in from light grey and darkens to ink while the line re-centres around whatever is already on screen. The words leave left to right as the rings fade out, all within 2.5 seconds.
scenes.build: `ring()` from components/rings.ts is a hair-thin TorusGeometry with a ShaderMaterial. The material discards fragments to make dashes and colours each one by its NDC x, so the gradient stays still while the ring rotates. `poseRing()` turns ellipse keys measured in pixels (semi-axis, aspect, roll, centre) into a rotation and scale. Each key is a monotone `glide()` curve. The headline comes from `line()` (one canvas-texture plane per word), with a custom layout that re-centres it every frame as gaps open.
scenes.reuse: Use it as a light, airy cold open for any one-line hook. Swap SENTENCE and the IN/OUT frames per word, and the ring colours. The ring shader (screen-space gradient plus dash discard) works anywhere you need orbit or loop lines. The ring keyframes were hand-measured from a reference film, so reshape them freely rather than copying the numbers.

scenes.title: Clock-dial counter to 30:00, then a fast 1–6 count
scenes.summary: A full-frame dial of 180 pale minor ticks and 18 slate major ticks grows in and steps round like a clock. Meanwhile a huge tabular counter rolls up to "30:00" with "minutes" under it. The clock slides off left and "its implementation took" builds in, with "implementation" in slate teal. The dial then blows outward past the frame edges and a large digit counts 1→6 in the centre, handing off to the next scene's "6 weeks".
scenes.build: Each tick ring is a THREE.InstancedMesh of unit quads arranged with `placeTicks()` (matrix compose per instance). Ring radius, tick length and rotation are `glide()` keys. The counter is a set of pre-built `label()` planes, one per distinct time string, using an "Inter Tnum" tabular-figures FontFace from `withInter()`. Only the current one is shown each frame. The grey→ink colour and blur go through `setLabel()` on the type shader in components/type.ts.
scenes.reuse: Borrow it for any "it only took X minutes" or time-based stat reveal. Swap the target time in `secs`, the caption, the follow-up line and the final count. The instanced tick dial is a strong reusable stopwatch or clock motif. The number swap at the end is tuned to cut into scene 03's "6", so drop it if your next scene isn't a number.

scenes.title: "6 weeks" on a hairline grid, zooming through to piling requirements
scenes.summary: A huge "6" is joined by "weeks", which is painted with a charcoal-to-slate gradient. The pair sits in a wide cell of a pale hairline grid while the frame pans and pulls back. At about 1.5s the pull-back zooms through into a finer grid with "+" crosses at the intersections. There, "Custom Pricing", "New Payment terms" and "New Compliance requirements" replace each other in place. Each one rises out with blur and the next rises in, while the camera keeps easing back and drifting.
scenes.build: `makeGrid()` builds full-length hairline quads plus cross marks. Its `setScale()` divides the line thickness by the group scale so hairlines stay 2px while the shot scales. There are two root groups (shot A, shot B) with a hard switch at f179 to fake the zoom-through. "weeks" uses the `paint` option of `label()` to fill the glyphs with a canvas gradient. The phrases are `line()` groups sized to measured pixel widths with `fit()`.
scenes.reuse: Good for a "the cost of the status quo" beat: a big duration or number, then the reasons it's that big, swapped in place. Change the number, the unit and the three phrases (keep the accent word per phrase in `inks`). The constant-width hairline grid trick works for any blueprint or graph-paper backdrop.

scenes.title: Isometric ground with a ring travelling a dashed route past popping tiles
scenes.summary: A true-isometric ground slides in from the top right as three stacked layers. The top layer is pale blue, gridded and lit by a soft glow, and the gaps between layers close as it lands. A pale iso ring travels a dashed white route from corner to corner. At each corner a white tile pops up from its lower-left corner with a slate icon (office building, box, team of people, storefront). "IT implementation" stands on a translucent card along the back edge, sheared to the iso baseline. The whole board drifts toward the lower left.
scenes.build: The ground layers are groups with `matrixAutoUpdate=false` and a basis matrix (ex/ey/ez) that projects ground (u,v) to an iso screen offset (HX=165, HY=95.3). Every rect, hairline and dash is a unit quad in ground space, and line thickness is corrected per axis with `across()`. Camera-facing pieces (nodes, ring, tiles) are positioned each frame through `projX/projY`. The tiles and icons are drawn in canvas 2D (`drawIcon`). The text card uses a hand-written skew Matrix4.
scenes.reuse: Use it to show an enterprise estate, a supply chain or a process map in iso without 3D models. Swap the icons in `drawIcon`, the route corners, the tile pop frames and the card text. The affine iso-group trick is the main takeaway. The specific icon drawings are template-specific.

scenes.title: "A change started in Salesforce" cascading down a department chain
scenes.summary: "A change" drifts left, then "started in [Salesforce cloud] Salesforce" slides in, with the real Salesforce cloud mark inline in the sentence. The words clear and the cloud grows and lifts away to the upper left. A hairline stem drops from it to a bracketed "Billing" tag. The view scrolls down one level at a time through "Finance" and "Compliance". Each level has big pale arcs, a sweeping connector to the right and an icon (receipt, invoice with $, shield with tick) on a ring node. Everything fades by the end.
scenes.build: `svgPlane()` (components/svg.ts) loads the Salesforce SVG through `ctx.manager` and rasterises it into a CanvasTexture. Arcs are custom `arcMesh()` ring-strip BufferGeometry. Each department level is a group offset by LEVEL px, and the whole chain scrolls on one glided `B` curve. The labels use `label()`, and the corner brackets are four tiny quads.
scenes.reuse: Borrow it for "one change ripples through X → Y → Z" or any downstream-impact explanation. Swap the logo SVG, the `depts` names and icons, and the copy. Don't copy the Salesforce mark into an unrelated video, because it is a third-party trademark standing in for an integration.

scenes.title: Glass slabs toppling like dominoes under "without breaking"
scenes.summary: "All without breaking" builds word by word in mid grey. Six thin grey glass slabs with white rims and dark outlines rise from below and topple to the left one after another like dominoes, flattening out of frame. The first line slides left and fades to a ghost. "years of custom logic." arrives over it with "custom logic." in teal, masked so the ghost line is wiped where the new one lands.
scenes.build: Each slab is a BoxGeometry with a canvas-textured face, nested in a shear group whose matrix is set per frame (`matrix.set(1, sin a, …)`). That gives a lean with the top edge kept level, not a rotation. The rise and fall are staggered `prog()` curves. The ghost-wipe uses the type shader's `maskX`/`maskSoft` uniforms from `setLabel()`.
scenes.reuse: Use it for fragility, "don't break things" or a chain-reaction line. Swap the two lines and the slab count and colours. The shear-matrix domino fall is a cheap, reusable motion. The `maskX` crossfade between two overlapping lines is worth borrowing too.

scenes.title: "That is where enterprise IT" → huge "gets stuck"
scenes.summary: "That is where enterprise IT" builds word by word, with gaps closing as it completes, and slowly recedes. Hard cut to a frame-filling slate "gets stuck" that lands oversized, keeps shrinking and blurs away. The outer letters are blurrier than the centre, like a shallow depth of field.
scenes.build: The first line uses `line()` with a shrinking `spread` term. "gets stuck" uses `letters()` (one plane per glyph) so `setLabel()` can blur each letter by its distance from centre (`edge ** 3`).
scenes.reuse: A quick two-card text beat. Swap both strings. The per-letter depth-of-field blur is the only idea not already shown elsewhere in this template.

scenes.title: "Multiple platforms" on a grid with logos flooding into slate cells
scenes.summary: "Multiple platforms" in slate sits in a double-width cell of a pale blue hairline grid with slate corner ticks, blurring in hard. The camera pulls back fast. Platform marks pop in on the diagonals around the text (a Z mark, HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, Workday) and their cells flood solid slate, with the marks turning white. Pale blue cells then check in further out. All of this happens in 1.5 seconds.
scenes.build: Everything is laid out in cell units inside one `board` group scaled by a glided `cell` px value. Grid hairline thickness is set to 3/c so lines stay crisp. Each mark has two textures (slate-tinted and white) from `svgTexture()` with a `fill` override, crossfaded as the tile's opacity floods in. The pop, flood and pale-cell timings are a frame table.
scenes.reuse: A strong, fast "works with / connects to" or "spread across tools" beat. Swap the PLATFORMS table (url, cell, pop and flood frames) for your own integrations and the two words. The dual-texture slate→white flood is the reusable trick. The logos are third-party trademarks, so replace them.

scenes.title: "Undocumented" typed behind a block caret, then "Teams trying to understand"
scenes.summary: "Undocumented" types itself huge, filling the frame width, behind a caret made of a 4×3 cluster of slate-blue blocks. The newest letter shows white on the dark block and the previous one grey. The camera pulls back while "decisions" in teal rises in beneath. The column scrolls up and away. "Teams trying to" rises word by word from below, and "understand" types out letter by letter under it as the pair recedes.
scenes.build: `letters()` gives per-glyph planes for the typing, and visibility is driven by a glided `typed` count. The caret is a group of coloured quads parented to the word and moved to the newest letter's x each frame. Each column's scale and y come from `glide()` keys. Each word of the second line rises on its own curve until it joins the line.
scenes.reuse: Use it for a "hidden knowledge" or "nobody wrote it down" beat, or any type-on headline that needs more character than a thin caret. Swap the words and the caret block palette (TONES).

scenes.title: Towers of outlined shapes tumble into a heap under "Everything else"
scenes.summary: "how one change / affects" rises in at the left beside two towers of pale blue outlined shapes (circles, clovers, triangles, rounded squares). The towers sway, give way and tumble into a heap along the bottom of the frame. The line is replaced by a centred "Everything else" that slowly scales up. A soft teal glow wells up from the bottom edge to hand off to the logo reveal.
scenes.build: There are four stroked shape textures from `shapeTexture()`. Each of the 10 shapes has start, mid and end keys (x, y, rotation) in a table, and motion is piecewise: a lean pivot from the floor, then a fall (outCubic x, inQuad y), then a settle. `bottomGlow()` from components/glow.ts is a radial-gradient canvas ellipse below the frame, driven by `set(strength, rise)`.
scenes.reuse: Use it for collapse, "it all falls apart" or knock-on-effects beats. Swap the words and the shape kinds and colours. Retune the SHAPES keys if you change the count. The bottom-glow handoff is a nice bridge into a product reveal.

scenes.title: Bar-by-bar logo build with tracking-in wordmark over a teal glow
scenes.summary: Over a teal glow welling up from the bottom, the Assemble mark builds left to right. Six translucent grey bars appear, then six mint→teal→navy gradient bars grow in, stepped down and to the right over them. At the same time the "Assemble" wordmark types in from wide tracking, each letter inking from grey to black as the spacing closes. The whole lockup settles back from 1.2× to rest.
scenes.build: `assembleLogo()` (components/assemble-logo.ts) builds the lockup at its measured pixel size: bar quads with their origin at the top edge, a gradient CanvasTexture for the front bars, and `letters()` for the wordmark with an animatable `track(em)`. The scene animates letter opacity and tint, `track()`, bar opacity and scaleY, and a scale about a pivot.
scenes.reuse: A clean product-name reveal after a problem section. Replace `assembleLogo()` with your own mark (any set of bars or shapes plus a `letters()` wordmark) and keep the timing pattern: back layer first, front layer grows, tracking closes, letters ink in. Don't reuse the Assemble mark itself.

scenes.title: AI composer: prompt types out, CSV dragged in as a chip, cursor clicks Send
scenes.summary: An AI-agent composer UI with model and workspace chips ("Claude Fable 5", "Default Workspace") and HubSpot and Salesforce connector chips. The prompt types itself in teal: "Build a Salesforce warm-account automation. Use the Accounts in…". A cursor drags an "accounts.csv" file card with an Excel icon into the box, where it becomes an inline chip. The rest of the brief types out over four lines. The camera then pushes in hard on the Send button and the cursor clicks it, turning it from pale to slate.
scenes.build: Every UI piece is a `panel()` canvas texture (components/ui.ts: `rrect`, `text`, `chevron`, `cursorPanel`). The typing uses per-character advance tables and the type shader's `maskX` uniform, converted from base px to world space through the camera transform (`toWorldX`). The camera is a scale+translate on the `ui` group from glided S/TX/TY keys. The file drag and the pointer are glided paths in base px.
scenes.reuse: Strong reference for any "you type a prompt and attach a file" product demo. Swap the prompt lines, the file name and icon, the connector chips and the Send-button colours. The maskX typing and the push-in-to-click camera are fully reusable. The copy and connector brands are specific to this product.

scenes.title: Agent transcript streaming in and whip-scrolling through tool calls
scenes.summary: Straight after Send, the agent's run streams in under the prompt bubble: "Thought for 1 seconds", terminal cards (ls / cat accounts.csv, env, curl describe), Read/Tool/Write rows (one marked ERROR), and a Salesforce change card with Cold→Warm before/after rows and "✓ APPLIED". Then come tables of governed change sets, a file tree, "Summary" bullets and the test list. The page scrolls slowly at first, whips through the middle and eases out on "Tests". A white wipe from the right clears it.
scenes.build: components/transcript.ts has block factories (`bubble`, `thought`, `terminal`, `toolRow`, `prose` with inline mono and bold runs, `bullets`, `heading`, `codeCard`, `changeCard`, `table`). Each draws one canvas plane at column width, and `layout()` stacks them. Scroll is one glided offset pinned to anchors (`D(id, screenY)`). Each block fades in when it first crosses the fold, precomputed per frame, with LATE/EARLY overrides. The wipe is a gradient plane.
scenes.reuse: The go-to reference for showing an AI agent or terminal run in a launch video. Rewrite the `B` block list for your own run (keep a mix of thought, terminal, tool-row and summary blocks) and re-anchor the scroll keys to your block ids. The transcript component is reusable as is. The Salesforce/Apex content is specific to this template.

scenes.title: Collaborator cursor drops an AWS node that expands into an architecture diagram
scenes.summary: A small "AWS" node card with a wire running off the right slides in, carried by a slate multiplayer cursor tagged "Assemble". The tag flies off to the upper right. The node opens into an architecture group while the view pulls back: a "Databricks" box, a dashed "Networking & Edge" group (VPC + Transit Gateway, CloudFront CDN, Application Load Balancer, outlined in purple) and a dashed "Microservices (EKS)" group (E-comm & Order Mgmt, Pricing & Promo Engine, Replenish & Store-Ops API, outlined in orange). Then it dissolves.
scenes.build: The card body and border are top-left-anchored quads resized every frame from glided W/H, with border thickness divided by scale. The child boxes and dashed groups are `panel()` textures revealed on a frame table. The collaborator cursor is two panels (label and arrow) on its own glided TX/TY path. The whole diagram is scaled and moved by S/X/Y keys.
scenes.reuse: Use it for "the agent understands your infrastructure" or any node-expands-into-subsystem diagram. Swap the labels, group titles, outline colours and icon. The named-cursor carry-in is a nice multiplayer and agent-presence device.

scenes.title: Stack of governed change cards landing on a timeline
scenes.summary: A timeline of governed Salesforce changes. Each new card lands on top of the stack as a pale blue placeholder that fills in, pushing the older ones down a slot: "Create 1 Account", "Create 1 Contact", "Create 1 Opportunity", "Update 3 Accounts", two "Create 1 Task". Each card has a "✓ APPLIED" badge, an orange "Compensating revert" or green "Fully reversible" pill, an "N applied" count and a "Revert" button. The stack then lifts away.
scenes.build: Each card is a `panel()` content texture plus a Salesforce logo plane plus a ghost placeholder panel that crossfades out. The stack position comes from summing `prog()` of every newer card (slide-down per landing), with a glided `top` offset. The data is a CARDS table with landing frames.
scenes.reuse: Good for an activity feed, audit log or "every change is reversible" beat. Swap the CARDS titles, subtitles and pill types, and the logo. The placeholder-then-fill landing pattern works for notifications or task lists too.

scenes.title: Agent-trace Gantt drawn in by a playhead as the timeline whips left
scenes.summary: An "Agent trace" Gantt chart with Query, Agent, Tools, Filesystem and Browser lanes and time ticks from 0:00 to 8:52. A fixed playhead near the right edge draws bars in as the timeline scrolls left, slowly at first and then very fast: navy agent blocks, teal "bash 0:23", "salesforce_create_record 1:15" and "salesforce_update_records 1:53" bars, then purple filesystem writes. The label column scrolls away, the teal glow rises from the bottom and the chart dissolves into it.
scenes.build: The lanes, grid and tick labels sit in a `tl` group translated by a glided offset. Each bar is a `panel()` whose geometry is anchored at its left edge, and `scale.x = clamp01((PLAYHEAD - screenX)/w)` draws it in as it passes the playhead. The opacity settles further back. The pinned label column is its own panel that starts scrolling after offset 479. `bottomGlow()` rises underneath.
scenes.reuse: Borrow it for any trace, timeline, CI run, job log or "everything the agent did" visual. Swap ROWS (names and colours), the BARS table and the TICKS. The playhead-draws-bars-while-scrolling trick is the reusable core.

scenes.title: "weeks coordinating [consultants / solution architects / internal teams]" word slot
scenes.summary: Over the teal glow, "instead of spending" builds word by word. It gives way to a slate "weeks" that inks to charcoal and shrinks, then "coordinating" types on after it letter by letter. A vertical word slot at the end of the line cycles "consultants" → "solution architects" → "internal teams" in slate, with neighbours shown pale above and below. The line slowly recedes and clears into the rising glow.
scenes.build: The "weeks" label, the `letters()` for "coordinating" and three slot labels sit in one group, re-centred on the typed width each frame. The slot is driven by a glided fractional index `slotIdx`. Each word's y offset is `-d * lineHeight`, and its tint and opacity come from its distance to the index. The glow is `bottomGlow()`.
scenes.reuse: Use it for the "instead of X" payoff line or any rotating-word tagline ("built for designers / engineers / teams"). Swap SLOT, the lead-in and the timing keys. The fractional-index word slot is the reusable piece.

scenes.title: Closing logo lockup over a swelling glow (repeat of the reveal)
scenes.summary: The teal glow swells up to fill the lower frame, then settles. The Assemble lockup builds exactly as in scene 11: grey bars, then gradient bars, with the wordmark tracking in and inking from grey to black. It holds while slowly receding, then shrinks and fades into the end line.
scenes.build: This is the scene 11 animation re-timed with `SHIFT = 602` (the same glide keys evaluated at F-602), plus a `tail` scale curve and an end fade. It uses `assembleLogo()` and `bottomGlow()` with a glided swell.
scenes.reuse: Only useful as an example of reusing a reveal clock for the closing lockup by shifting the frame. For the logo build itself, study scene 11.

scenes.title: "Learn more at" → URL glides to centre and "/today" types on
scenes.summary: Over a full teal bottom glow, "Learn more at" builds word by word in charcoal, and the bold black URL "assemble.ai" types on letter by letter after it. The lead-in blurs away to the left, the URL glides to centre, and "/today" types onto the end of it. It holds to the end of the film.
scenes.build: The lead-in is a `line()` and the URL is a `letters()` group with per-letter reveal frames (URL_T), including a pause before "/today". Two glided x curves (L for the lead-in, AL for the URL) hand the line off from left-aligned to centred. The glow is `bottomGlow().set(1, 0, 0.08)`.
scenes.reuse: A simple, polished end card for any launch. Swap the lead-in, the URL string and the URL_T timings (one entry per character, including the delayed path suffix). Re-tune AL so the final URL is centred for its new width.
